Duties include but are not limited to: Possesses knowledge related to the physiology associated with various anesthesia techniques and surgical interventions. Assesses and prepare patients for procedures appropriately. Performs clinical assessment of the patient and readily recognizes contraindication for anesthesia and/or surgical intervention.

Applies the appropriate post sedation scoring and assesses the patient's postoperative status to include cardiovascular and respiratory systems and airway management needs, neurological system, hemodynamic stability, pain, and comfort needs and mental status, implementing appropriate interventions to maintain or return all physiological system to baseline or above.

Maintains knowledge of current American Society of Peri anesthesia Nurses (ASPAN) standards, Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Directives and service level standard operating procedures (SOPs). Responsible for ensuring comprehensive documenting of all phases of care and is timely, complete, and accurate in the electronic health record (EHR).

May be required to perform on-call duties.

Other duties as assigned VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: Full time, four 10-hr shifts with on-call duties, Monday to Friday, 8:00am - 6:30pm.

The incumbent must be a mature, flexible, sensible individual capable or working effectively in stressful situation, able to shift priorities based on needs of the organization. The incumbent who provides off-site training may be required to travel occasionally. This position potentially requires flexibility in schedule and assignments.

Major Duties and Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Serves as the facility's clinical expert in wound, ostomy, continence, and pressure injury management, providing advanced nursing care for patients with complex wound care needs.

Coordinates and manages comprehensive wound care services by developing, implementing, and evaluating individualized, evidence-based treatment plans across the continuum of care.

Provides expert wound care consultations and collaborates with physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, rehabilitation staff, and other interdisciplinary team members to optimize patient outcomes.

Demonstrates clinical leadership by applying advanced critical thinking, sound clinical judgment, and evidence-based practices to complex wound management decisions. Leads interdisciplinary efforts to prevent and reduce hospital-acquired pressure injuries through risk assessment, surveillance, and implementation of prevention strategies.

Collects, monitors, analyzes, and reports wound care and pressure injury quality data; collaborates with Quality Management, Patient Safety, and interdisciplinary committees to support performance improvement initiatives Serves as an active member of the Interdisciplinary Pressure Injury Committee (IPIC) and other specialty committees to improve wound care processes and organizational outcomes.

Develops, delivers, and evaluates education and competency-based training programs for clinical staff to ensure consistent application of current evidence-based wound care practices. Assists in the evaluation, selection, procurement, and implementation of wound care products, therapies, and supplies to support timely, effective patient care.

Collaborates in the development, implementation, revision, and evaluation of wound care policies, procedures, clinical practice guidelines, and standards of care.

Maintains accountability for program-level wound care outcomes by evaluating clinical performance measures, identifying improvement opportunities, and implementing sustainable quality initiatives.

Functions as an expert clinical resource, mentor, and patient advocate, demonstrating advanced leadership, technical proficiency, and professional expertise in the management of complex wound care cases.

Responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing and/or supervising direct patient care. Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care.

Administers medications and procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team. Core elements of performance include knowledge and active participation in the unit/program level quality improvement process and initiatives as well as customer service programs.

The Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based care to assigned patients and oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants, as appropriate to the setting.

The nurse will assist in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization consultation. Demonstrates leadership in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others. Evaluates practice in an ongoing process, based on best evidence.

Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement. Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals. Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team. Partners with others to effect change and produce optimal outcomes.

Supports colleagues through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care. Shares educational findings, experiences, and ideas with peers. Questions clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based care. Participates in activities and strategies to sustain an evidence-based-practice culture.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING DAY TO DAY As a Nurse (Consultant), you will use your knowledge and experience to optimize business results and customer experience by: Serving as a clinical consultant and subject matter expert in the development, implementation, and evaluation of complex healthcare and public health programs.

Providing clinical expertise and recommendations on healthcare policies, legislative proposals, quality measurement initiatives, and nursing practice standards. Leading special studies, program evaluations, and healthcare assessments to measure the effectiveness and quality of clinical services and healthcare delivery systems.

Collaborating with healthcare professionals, government officials, and stakeholders to develop solutions, improve health programs, and support organizational goals.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR Basic Qualifications: Education Requirement: A graduate or higher-level degree, bachelor's degree, associate degree, or diploma from an accredited professional nursing educational program is required.

This education must have been accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education(external link), Council on Accreditation of Nurse Anesthesia Educational Programs(external link), Accreditation Commission for Midwifery Education(external link), or an accrediting body recognized by the U.S.

Department of Education(external link) at the time the degree was obtained. Degree from Foreign Nursing School: Official certification from the Commission on Graduates of Foreign Nursing Schools (external link) is required for individuals who graduated from foreign nursing schools.

AND Licensure Requirement: For all grade levels and positions, applicants must have passed the National Council Licensure Examination(external link).

In addition, they must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration as a professional nurse from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States.

In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Minimum Qualifications: You must have one year of specialized experience to perform successfully the duties of the position.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service performing ALL of the following: Developing, implementing, and evaluating standard operating procedures (SOPs), program plans, and workflows to improve efficiency, consistency, and service delivery outcomes; Monitoring and analyzing program performance data, including productivity, turnaround times, and quality assurance metrics, and preparing reports and dashboards to inform leadership decision-making; Identifying and resolving complex operational, administrative, and customer service issues, including responding to agency complaints, resolving vendor issues, and implementing corrective actions; and Overseeing billing, financial reconciliation, and resource management activities, ensuring alignment between services provided, funding, and interagency agreements (IAAs) and Statements of Work (SOWs).

Documenting experience: IN DESCRIBING YOUR EXPERIENCE, PLEASE BE CLEAR AND SPECIFIC. WE WILL NOT MAKE ASSUMPTIONS REGARDING YOUR EXPERIENCE. Qualifications are based on breadth/level of experience.

In addition to describing duties performed, applicants must provide the exact dates of each period of employment (from MM/YY to MM/YY) and the number of hours worked per week if part time.

As qualification determinations cannot be made when resumes do not include the required information, failure to provide this information may result in disqualification. Applicants are encouraged to use the USAJOBS Resume Builder to develop their federal resume.

Do not copy and paste the duties, specialized experience, or occupational application questionnaire from this announcement into your resume as that will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position.

In accordance with Office of Personnel Management policy, federal employees are assumed to have gained experience by performing duties and responsibilities appropriate for their official series and grade level as described in their position description.

Experience that would not normally be part of the employee's position is creditable, however, when documented by satisfactory evidence, such as a signed memorandum from the employee's supervisor or an SF-50 or SF-52 documenting an official detail or other official assignment.

The documentation must indicate whether the duties were performed full time or, if part time, the "percentage of times" the other duties were performed. It is expected that this documentation is included in the employee's official personnel record.

In order to receive credit for experience in your resume that is not within the official series and grade level of your official position, you must provide a copy of the appropriate documentation of such experience as indicated above.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through national Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; community; student; social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to gain employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

If such experience is on a part-time basis, you must provide the average number of hours worked per week as well as the beginning and ending dates of the experience so it can be fully credited. OPM Qualification General Policies Website

Duties The Nursing, GEC Nurse Manager (NM) is a registered professional nurse Responsible for the assessment, planning, provision and evaluation of nursing care on inpatient and outpatient services. NM provides 24/7 responsibility and accountability including weekends, and holidays.

Responsible and accountable for the management and supervision of all nursing staff personnel on all tours of duty.

Executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex client Responsible for directing and organizing the unit specific orientation, training and development of staff and for directing, supervising, and evaluating their performance.

Accountable for the provision of direct patient care and for the delivery of quality nursing care during times when the unit staffing is low and necessary to provide safe care to the veterans. Functions as nursing role model, educator, practitioner and manager, providing leadership to an interdisciplinary team.

Demonstrates the knowledge and skills necessary to provide care appropriate to the age-related needs of patients served in the assigned area of practice. This knowledge includes understanding changes associated with aging and principles of growth and development relevant to the adult and geriatric population.

Responsible for providing leadership in delivering and improving care through the collaboration with others. May receive a variety of additional assignments or special projects to either meet the needs of the Medical Center or designed for the growth of the individual.

Accountable and responsible for possessing the knowledge and skill to communicate and interact appropriately and courteously with all internal and external customers. Will maintain confidentiality of electronic, written and verbal patient/employee information.

Demonstrate working practices that include adherence to infection control standards and the safe use and operation of equipment. The NM will treat customers in a courteous and helpful manner that indicates dignity and respect. Will respond to customer requests in a timely manner.

Will be courteous, thoughtful, and caring in all interactions with patients, family members, visitors, and staff. Will use tact, discretion and patience when explaining policies and procedures and/or when assisting in finding an answer to a problem.

Displays a helpful, proactive attitude toward customers by answering questions and resolving problems to enhance customer satisfaction. Accepts assignments willingly, volunteers to help others, and works cooperatively and effectively with co-workers and supervisors displaying a helpful, positive attitude.

Consistently practices customer service performance expectations consistent with VHA ICARE values. All other duties as assigned. Functions as a clinical expert and is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing or supervising direct patient care.

Assesses, plans, implements, and evaluates delivery of care based on age specific components. Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care.

Degree or diploma from a professional nursing program approved by the legally designated State accrediting agency at the time the program was completed by the applicant.

Active, current registration as a professional nurse in a State, District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States.

This definition of professional nursing experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify.

The Outpatient Behavioral Health (BH) Registered Nurse (RN) executes position responsibilities to improve Veteran and organizational outcomes.

The psychiatric BH RN executes their position duties by providing patient-centered, recovery-oriented principles, telemental health, community-based care, and self-awareness when caring for Veterans living with BH conditions.

The BH RN actively engages in interdisciplinary team huddles and meetings, uses therapeutic communication techniques, de-escalation practices, recovery-oriented language, and educates Veterans, their families, and significant others on illnesses, medications, and treatment plans.

The BH RN assists and/or directs safety concern resolution and collaborates with program leadership to help improve Veteran and program outcomes, liaising with Inpatient BH Units, develops content as well as facilitates nurse-led psychoeducational groups, and directs teams response to psychiatric and medical emergencies.

The BH RN documents assessments, risk screens, measurement-based care tools, clinical reminders, and Veteran care plans following facility policy, maintaining professional boundaries and acting in the Veteran's best interest.

The registered nurse (RN) assigned to the outpatient Behavioral Health team collaborates with interdisciplinary treatment teams in the delivery and coordination of comprehensive care to Veterans receiving outpatient behavioral health services.

The RN may work in, be assigned to, or provide cross-coverage for any Behavioral Health Service (BHS) program, Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs), or facility under the El Paso VA Health Care System based on patient care needs and operational requirements.

Assignments may include, but are not limited to, the Behavioral Health Access Team (BHAT), Primary Care Mental Health Integration (PCMHI), Behavioral Health Interdisciplinary Program (BHIP), Somatic Treatments (i.e Esketamine, etc.), Hospital Liaison, Intensive Community Mental Health Recovery (ICMHR), Housing and Urban Development-VA Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH).

The RN must maintain a current, valid, and unrestricted driver's license and possess the ability to safely operate a Government Services Administration (GSA) vehicle.

Driving responsibilities may include travel between CBOCs & Main VA Facility within the El Paso VA Health Care System, community-based and home visits, outreach activities, and minimal transportation of Veterans when necessary and consistent with VA policy and operational requirements.

This requirement supports the RN's responsibility to provide coverage and services across BHS programs, community settings, CBOCs, and other facilities that fall under the El Paso VA Health Care System.

Behavioral Health Services (BHS) provides a comprehensive range of services, including walk-in/same-day access, crisis assessment and management, group programming, evidence-based treatments, tele-mental health services, medication management, case management/Mental Health Treatment Coordinator (MHTC) services, counseling for couples and families, psychological assessment, outreach, and other behavioral health services.

The responsibilities of the Behavioral Health Registered Nurse (BH RN) include, but are not limited to, conducting risk assessments, triage, and clinical nursing services for Veterans seeking or receiving behavioral health care.

The BH RN addresses Secure Messaging (SM), Message Managers (MM), and other Veteran care requests within established facility policy and standards for timeliness, responding directly within the RN's scope of practice and appropriately routing, reassigning, or escalating requests to the appropriate team, provider, or service when indicated.

The RN reviews diagnostic and laboratory results, discusses abnormal findings with the referring or responsible provider, and communicates normal results to Veterans and/or caregivers, as appropriate. Other duties as assigned.

Ferien
Abschalten vom intensiven Arbeitsalltag - Ihre körperliche und geistige Erholung ist wichtig. Sie sind ein aktiver, geselliger Mensch? Unser Freizeitclub PDGR-AKTIV, der allen Mitarbeitenden offen steht, organisiert vielseitige Aktivitäten - ob Besuche im Bündner Kunstmuseum, Paintball-Wettkämpfe oder das Erklimmen verschiedener bekannter Bündner Berge - es hat für jeden etwas dabei. Fitnessräume

Gesundes Essen

Apfel- und Birnenaktion
Traditionsgemäss sorgt unsere 3-wöchige Apfel- und Birnenaktion im Herbst für eine energiereiche Zwischenverpflegung.
E-Bikes
